prompt.context: Your client is Royal Cinemas, a NYC theater chain. Their revenue has been badly hurt by decreasing ticket sales, which are at their lowest point since 1996 for both the chain and the industry at large. Royal Cinemas is interested in converting their theaters into luxury cinemas.
prompt.question: Should Royal Cinemas convert their theaters into luxury cinemas?

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeframe for entry if they decide to proceed?
clarifying_info.a: If they choose to enter the market, they intend to enter immediately.

clarifying_info.q: How does Royal Cinemas currently price tickets and concessions?
clarifying_info.a: Currently prices tickets and concessions the same as competitors.

clarifying_info.q: How many competitors are in the NYC luxury cinema market?
clarifying_info.a: There are fewer than 5 major players in NYC.
Revenue has been steadily declining for 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does Royal Cinemas currently have?
Has Royal Cinemas previously attempted to enter the luxury space?
clarifying_info.a: No, they have not previously attempted to enter the luxury space.

clarifying_info.q: Is there information on the luxury market size and growth?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there is information on this — let me see how you would like to approach the problem from a high level first, and then I will share it.

exhibits.title: U.S. Cinema Market Share: Standard vs. Luxury
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the trend of market share over time for standard (non-luxury) theaters versus luxury theaters in the U.S.
exhibits.data: Luxury theaters are gaining market share over time while standard theaters are losing market share; specific percentage values are shown on the chart.

exhibits.title: Royal Cinema: Current Standard State vs. Luxury State Comparison
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side table comparing key operating metrics between the current standard state and a proposed luxury state across peak and off-peak periods.
exhibits.data: # Theatre Locations: 10 (both); # Screens/theatre: 10 (both); # Seats/screen: 150 (standard) vs 65 (luxury); # Showings/week Peak: 20 (both), Off-Peak: 40 (both); Ticket Price: $10 (standard) vs $15 (luxury); Avg Concession Spend/person: $10 (standard) vs $35 (luxury); Capacity Peak: 80% (standard) vs 90% (luxury), Off-Peak: 20% (standard) vs 30% (luxury)

framework: Financial Implications: Costs (renovations, equipment, shutdown costs if location unprofitable) and Revenues (ticket pricing, concession pricing, number of customers, number of items purchased) — ultimately calculate breakeven point
Market Attractiveness: Size and growth of the luxury cinema market; consumer tastes and preferences; whether the target customer is the same as or different from current customers
Competitive Analysis: Key players and their market share, how share has changed over time, differentiating factors Royal Cinemas could offer, likely competitor response to RC's entry

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, what does the market data tell you about the luxury cinema opportunity?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate identifies the clear trend: luxury theaters are gaining market share while standard theaters are losing share, suggesting the luxury market is a promising prospect. An excellent candidate also notes that the U.S. market data may not be fully representative of the NYC market specifically.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 2, calculate the expected weekly revenue for the current standard state and the proposed luxury state. How does this influence your view on whether RC should enter the luxury market?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate correctly calculates weekly revenue for both states and identifies that luxury revenue is materially higher despite fewer seats, because higher prices and higher actual capacity offset the seat reduction. An excellent candidate also discusses qualitative pros and cons: standard state benefits from existing brand familiarity but struggles against streaming competition; luxury state offers superior experience but capacity projections are assumptions that may overstate the opportunity.

math.setup: Revenue = (# Locations) x (# Screens) x (# Seats) x (# Showings) x (Ticket Price + Avg Concession Spend) x Capacity. Calculate Peak and Off-Peak separately, then sum.
steps: Standard Off-Peak: 10 x 10 x 150 x 40 x $20 x 20% = $2,400,000
Luxury Off-Peak: 10 x 10 x 65 x 40 x $50 x 30% = $3,900,000
Revenue uplift: $9,750,000 - $7,200,000 = $2,550,000 more per week in luxury state
math.answer: Standard state weekly revenue: $7.2M; Luxury state weekly revenue: $9.75M. Luxury generates ~35% more weekly revenue despite 57% fewer seats per screen, supporting the case for conversion.

questions.prompt: Royal Cinemas would like to know how long it will take to recoup their conversion and renovation costs. Calculate the payback period.
questions.guidance: A strong candidate calculates the payback period correctly. An excellent candidate also notes that ~5 months seems very short and questions whether the assumptions (especially the capacity projections) are realistic, and may flag the additional revenue loss during the renovation period.

math.setup: Payback Period = Initial Investment / Net Weekly Cash Flow. Net Weekly Cash Flow = Weekly Revenue - Weekly Variable Costs. Variable costs are given as 50% of weekly revenue.
math.answer: Approximately 20.5 weeks, or roughly 5 months. This is a very short payback period — an excellent candidate will flag that this may be overly optimistic given that the capacity projections are assumptions.

brainstorming.prompt: Royal Cinemas is aware that it will need to compete with other successful luxury cinemas in New York City. How might it differentiate itself in this space?

categories.name: Concessions
ideas: Partnership with a well-known food market, restaurant, or celebrity chef
In-theater waiter service (consider food/drink minimum spend to protect concession revenue)

categories.name: Environment
ideas: Work cafe with wifi in lobby area to drive dwell time and incremental spend
Aromatherapy or enhanced sensory elements in theater

categories.name: Added Content
ideas: Regular talk-backs or Q&As with film crew and directors
Special film shorts or curated content screened before each movie

categories.name: Partnerships & Other
ideas: Partnerships with luxury hotel chains for bundled experiences
Partnerships with gyms or wellness brands for co-marketing
Loyalty program targeted at high-value luxury consumers

recommendation: Royal Cinemas should proceed with converting their theaters into luxury cinemas.

The luxury cinema market is projected to grow steadily, luxury conversion would increase weekly revenue from $7.2M to $9.75M with operational costs held constant, and the payback period on the $100M investment is approximately 5 months — a compelling financial case. There are also plentiful differentiation opportunities to compete effectively in the NYC luxury market.
risks: Competition with established luxury cinema players already in NYC
Revenue loss from theaters/screens closed during renovation period
Capacity projections in the luxury model are assumptions — if actual utilization is lower, the revenue uplift will be overstated
Heavy reliance on concession revenue; a minimum spend policy should be considered
Brand confusion risk if RC maintains a mix of standard and luxury locations
Ongoing threat from streaming services reducing in-person cinema attendance overall
next_steps: Ensure organizational structure and staffing are ready to support a luxury cinema operation
Develop a marketing strategy to attract luxury consumers and retain loyal existing customers
Evaluate cost-effective, on-brand partnership opportunities for concessions and hospitality elements
